solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After month, a class is to break up

parts.note: SEP is the calendar abbreviation for September
taken as written
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A school class plans to disband once the month is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After month' puts the month first, with 'a class' following it.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to split apart or part company, a straightforward synonym of break up.

clue.text: Friend of Pooh and mine keeping leg moving

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about and settle in a fresh order
something keeping another holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
the letters of leg, rearranged

explanation.surface: A character from Winnie-the-Pooh appears beside a mine where a leg is in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged leg goes inside PIT, giving PI-GLE-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Piglet is the small, timid pig who is Winnie-the-Pooh's closest companion in A. A. Milne's stories.

clue.text: In secluded oasis, ayahs obey me!

indicators.note: in signals that the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of secluded, all of oasis and the start of ayahs

explanation.surface: A colonial employer in a remote desert retreat commands the nannies to obey.
explanation.walkthrough: An ayah is a nursemaid or maid in South Asia, a word from the British Raj.
explanation.definitionFit: Do as I say is the stock command demanding compliance, an idiom equivalent to obey me.

parts.note: de is French for of
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A demonstration by a doctor from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a short, informal word for a public demonstration, which is a protest.

parts.note: two fools, each an ass
in means at home

explanation.surface: A murderer turns out to be a pair of idiotic twins staying indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twin' doubles the word for fool, so ASS appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, especially one who kills a prominent person for political motives.

definitions.note: read cryptically as two words, in tent
definitions.meaning: first meaning: split as two words, staying under canvas
second meaning: an aim or purpose

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two and it describes where a camper sleeps; read whole, it is a purpose. The question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: An intent is an aim or purpose held in mind, which is a goal.

parts.note: a worker is a type of ant; 'perhaps' marks it as an example
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A worker joins forces with a single adversary.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who is against something, so an opponent of a policy or cause.

clue.text: Umpire at home with English and Polish

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an umpire
in means at home
E is the abbreviation for English; with simply adds it

explanation.surface: A match official relaxes indoors with Englishmen and Poles.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish is capitalised to look like the nationality; it is the verb meaning to improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine something is to improve it by small changes, much as one would polish it.

clue.text: Say incorrectly how to address gallery founder's daughter?

definitions.text: how to address gallery founder's daughter?
definitions.note: read cryptically as two words, Miss Tate
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Henry Tate founded the Tate Gallery

explanation.walkthrough: The sugar magnate Henry Tate founded London's Tate Gallery; an unmarried daughter would be addressed with the title Miss before the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To misstate is to give a false or inaccurate account of something, which is saying it incorrectly.

parts.note: f is forte, the musical term for loud
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Things go wrong after a loud explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the trouble after the loud letter. Bomb is the informal verb for a flop, not an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: To bomb is slang for to flop badly, so it means to fail.

indicators.note: not quite finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A young lad fails to get to the end of his solo.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, so a boy in relation to his parents.

clue.text: Lights showing seabirds east of territory, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
in an across answer east is to the right, so the birds come after the other piece

parts.note: land is territory
terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: Lights reveal seabirds flying to the east of a stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanterns are portable lamps in a protective case, so they are lights.

clue.text: Dishes of rice to stir so frenziedly

indicators.note: doing something frenziedly is wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Rice dishes that need stirring furiously, an accurate description of the cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder sits in the clue next to the definition, which really is cooked by stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: A risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock, so risottos are rice dishes.

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A thin period comes just before the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Lean looks like an adjective for thin; it is the verb meaning to incline.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend towards something is to incline or lean that way.

clue.text: Put up with some venom in a testimony

indicators.note: with some says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: spans the end of venom, in, a and the start of testimony

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a spiteful witness statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' looks like one phrase meaning tolerate, but the definition stops at 'Put up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a candidate is to propose them for election, which is to nominate them.

indicators.note: brought back suggests a return journey, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: Grass is carried back to feed cud-chewing animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer chew the cud, so they belong to the ruminants along with cattle and sheep.

clue.text: Vicar in park, over the hill

indicators.note: in a down answer over means placed above, so the park piece sits on top

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a park
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An elderly clergyman, past his prime, is sitting in the park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the hill' reads as the idiom for old, but over is a placement signal and the hill gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a Church of England priest in charge of a parish, broadly the same role as a vicar.

clue.text: Streaks of light bun, a mess when splattered

indicators.note: something splattered is scattered messily, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Streaks appear on a bun after it has been messily smeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a ray of sunlight, so sunbeams are shafts or streaks of light.

indicators.note: something ravaged is wrecked and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A district of London is devastated in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is a district and borough in west London, famous for its film studios.

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Someone's self-esteem is, for instance, nonexistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is a person's sense of their own worth and importance, which is self-esteem.

parts.note: taken as written; that the four letters also run consecutively across these words is a coincidence of the charade
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles along slowly inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to move very slowly and carefully, a small step at a time.

clue.text: Order to stop being misery to audience

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard by listeners, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: woe is misery

explanation.surface: A shout for silence because the misery is being performed to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the call used to make a horse halt, so a command to stop.

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An extended play record is expanded to carry a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Long describes something stretched out in length or time, the sense of extended.

clue.text: Cuts thin pants to reverse seamstress's work?

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or badly done, so the letters are in poor order and need rearranging

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone slices thin trousers in order to undo a seamstress's sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like the noun for trousers (or, in Britain, underpants); it is slang for poor, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress stitches, so to undo that work is to unpick the stitches, which is to unstitch.

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A well-known elderly woman turns out not to be from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' looks like it removes something, but here it is simply part of the build.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of note is notable or distinguished, which is to say well known or famous.

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, short for charwoman
's stands for is
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady's mother has real allure.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as possessive but is expanded to the word is. A char is an old British term for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling charm that inspires devotion, the personal appeal of a magnetic person.
